chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is treated with ATPase enzyme / H2O?
questions.explanation: Treating Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) with ATPase enzyme / H2O yields ADP + Inorganic phosphate (Pi) + 30.5 kJ/mol energy. Rationale: Hydrolysis of terminal phosphoanhydride bond relieves electrostatic repulsion and increases resonance stabilization.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of D-Glucose into Glucose-6-phosphate + ADP?
questions.explanation: To convert D-Glucose into Glucose-6-phosphate + ADP, the appropriate reagent is ATP / Hexokinase enzyme. Rationale: Hexokinase transfers a phosphate group from ATP to glucose C6, trapping glucose inside the cell.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is treated with Aldolase enzyme?
questions.explanation: Treating Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate with Aldolase enzyme yields Dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) + Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (GAP). Rationale: Enzymatic reverse-aldol cleavage splits the 6-carbon bisphosphate into two 3-carbon phosphorylated trioses.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 3-Ketoacyl-CoA into Fatty acyl-CoA (shortened by 2 carbons) + Acetyl-CoA?
questions.explanation: To convert 3-Ketoacyl-CoA into Fatty acyl-CoA (shortened by 2 carbons) + Acetyl-CoA, the appropriate reagent is Coenzyme A (CoA-SH) / Thiolase enzyme. Rationale: Thiolase catalyzes a retro-Claisen condensation, cleaving two-carbon acetyl-CoA from the fatty acid chain.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Pyruvate + Coenzyme A is treated with NAD+ / Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex?
questions.explanation: Treating Pyruvate + Coenzyme A with NAD+ / Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex yields Acetyl-CoA + CO2 + NADH. Rationale: Multi-enzyme complex decarboxylates pyruvate, transferring the acetyl group to CoA and reducing NAD+.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Oxaloacetate + Acetyl-CoA into Citrate + Coenzyme A (CoA-SH)?
questions.explanation: To convert Oxaloacetate + Acetyl-CoA into Citrate + Coenzyme A (CoA-SH), the appropriate reagent is Citrate synthase enzyme / H2O. Rationale: Acetyl-CoA enol intermediate attacks oxaloacetate carbonyl, followed by thioester hydrolysis to form citrate.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: Which starting material will react with NAD+ / Isocitrate dehydrogenase to yield Alpha-Ketoglutarate + CO2 + NADH as the major product?
questions.explanation: Isocitrate reacts with NAD+ / Isocitrate dehydrogenase to yield Alpha-Ketoglutarate + CO2 + NADH. Rationale: Oxidation of secondary alcohol to beta-keto acid followed by spontaneous decarboxylation yields alpha-ketoglutarate.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Alanine + Alpha-Ketoglutarate is treated with PLP-dependent Alanine transaminase?
questions.explanation: Treating Alanine + Alpha-Ketoglutarate with PLP-dependent Alanine transaminase yields Pyruvate + L-Glutamate. Rationale: Pyridoxal phosphate coenzyme forms a Schiff base, transferring the amino group from alanine to alpha-ketoglutarate.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: Which starting material will react with NAD+ + H2O / Glutamate dehydrogenase to yield Alpha-Ketoglutarate + NH4+ + NADH as the major product?
questions.explanation: L-Glutamate reacts with NAD+ + H2O / Glutamate dehydrogenase to yield Alpha-Ketoglutarate + NH4+ + NADH. Rationale: Oxidative deamination releases free ammonium ion and regenerates the citric acid cycle intermediate alpha-ketoglutarate.

questions.chapter_title: The Organic Chemistry of Metabolic Pathways
questions.question: What is the expected major product when L-Malate is treated with NAD+ / Malate dehydrogenase?
questions.explanation: Treating L-Malate with NAD+ / Malate dehydrogenase yields Oxaloacetate + NADH + H+. Rationale: Final step of the citric acid cycle oxidizes secondary alcohol to ketone, regenerating oxaloacetate.
